data.title: Treasury Yields, Dollar Fall as Risk Aversion Grips Wall Street — Market Talk
data.description:
0913 ET - Treasury yields and the dollar decline as investors rotate away from risky assets into the safety of bonds. The hype around Anthropic's blockbuster IPO fades as markets worry about AI's lofty ambitions. The decline in yields happens even as investors expect higher interest rates by the Fed to tame inflation. Brent crude is stable around $91. The WSJ Dollar Index falls 0.3%, with the greenback weakening 0.7% versus the yen. The 10-year yield slips below 5% to 4.972%. The two-year is at 4.675%, down from 4.777% yesterday. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)Andrew Kenningham works for Capital Economics. "France's Fiscal Arithmetic Remains Worrying — Market Talk," at 1440 GMT on Thursday, incorrectly said Kenningham works for Oxford Economics.

0907 ET - Credit spreads on euro corporate bonds widen as investors flee from risk assets towards safe-haven assets due to concerns about a possible slowdown in the artificial intelligence industry, LBBW's credit analysts say in a note. "Given the ongoing uncertainty, we do not expect a significant narrowing of spreads in the short term, but rather a sideways trend at the current elevated level." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0855 ET - The euro should gradually recover against the dollar next year, UBS Global Wealth Management analysts say in a note. Euro short positioning--bets on the currency falling--looks stretched, they say. The potential passage of a French budget should help the euro, although a lasting recovery is more likely after the French presidential elections in the second quarter of 2027, they say. Lower oil prices should bring down inflation, meanwhile. "As the policy debate shifts from hikes toward a prolonged pause and eventually easing, the dollar should lose support." The euro rises 0.3% to $1.0994, having reached a 19-month low of $1.0952 on Wednesday, according to LSEG. UBS expects the euro to reach $1.16 by September 2027, although it no longer anticipates a move to $1.20. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0852 ET - The value of Canada's gold assets reached a record high last year, and was the largest contributor the country's natural-resource wealth after energy. Statistics Canada data shows the dollar value of Canada's natural-resource wealth fell 7% to C$1.234 trillion in 2025. Energy resource value totaled C$583 billion, down C$250 billion from 2024 thanks to lower prices. Crude bitumen accounted for more than one-third of natural-resource value at C$430 billion. The value of mineral resources rose by C$162 billion to C$481 billion in 2025, while gold accounting for C$210 billion of that compared with C$83 billion in 2024. Gold prices hit a record early in 2026 but have retreated. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

0844 ET - Canadian shoppers may be showing signs of fatigue, or simply pausing spending ahead of the holiday season. Statistics Canada's early tally of retail sales points to a 1.5% drop on-month in October, which would be the sharpest fall since February 2025. That would mark a soft start to 4Q after sales rose 1.2% in 3Q. Sales rose 0.8% in September, a tick stronger that the 0.7% rise economists expected. That followed upwardly revised growth of 1.4% in August. September's advance was led by sales at gas stations on the back of higher fuel prices. Stripping out gas stations and sales for the month edged up 0.1%. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

0728 ET - Efforts by the U.K. to improve ties with the European Union are boosting sterling, Ebury's Matthew Ryan says in a note. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said at the EU-U.K. summit in Brussels that people across the U.K. will benefit from a "really significant" agreement with the EU. Sterling rises 0.1% versus the dollar to $1.3100. The euro falls 0.1% against sterling to 0.8370 pounds. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0725 ET - The dollar could suffer against core G-10 currencies if the selloff in AI-related stocks continues, MUFG Bank's Derek Halpenny writes in a note. Support for the U.S. economy from AI has been a key factor in intensifying concerns over elevated inflation and boosting expectations for interest-rate hikes, he says. If the selloff continues, the growth outlook could weaken and inflation expectations could fall, he adds. "There is still close to three Federal Reserve rate hikes priced which could quickly look disconnected from what's happening in the rest of the financial markets." The DXY dollar index trades flat at 103.912. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)Ether was trading up 1.8% at $1,793. "Ether Could Hold Above $1,700 if Accumulation by Large Holders Persists — Market Talk," at 1243 GMT on Nov. 19, misstated the price.

0632 ET - The cost of protecting euro-denominated credit against default rises as investors become more cautious due to fears about a potential slowdown in AI growth. Recent announcements about tighter regulations on U.S. chip sales to Asia are adding to existing fears around massive spending by artificial intelligence companies, Raffi Boyadjian, XM lead market analyst says in a note. The iTraxx Europe Crossover index of euro high-yield credit default swaps rises 9 basis points to 315bps, S&P Global Market Intelligence data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0533 ET - The Japanese yen is best positioned to benefit from risk aversion stemming from concerns over the sustainability of lofty valuations in artificial-intelligence stocks, MUFG Bank's Derek Halpenny says in a note. "An AI risk-off in magnitude would be disinflationary and that would help improve the outlook for the yen." If U.S. yields fall, global yields could also drop, but Japan now offers higher yields than before, he says. The yen is also a safe haven. The dollar falls 0.6% to a one-week low of 158.69 yen, according to LSEG. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0514 ET - Yields on U.K. and eurozone government bonds drop sharply due to strong demand for safe-haven assets as the tech sector selloff intensifies. Japan's Datasection cut its annual revenue forecast considerably this week, adding to concerns about the future profitability of artificial intelligence companies. "The slightest bit of bad news is sending shivers down the spines of tech investors as some fear the good times could be over," AJ Bell's Russ Mould says in a note. Ten-year gilt yields and 10-year Bund yields fall to a one-week low of 5.240%, and 3.317%, respectively, according to Tradeweb data. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: ICE Canola Futures Softer
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting small losses Friday morning as values continued to chop around in narrow, rangebound trade.

The January contract was down $2.50 at C$774.50 per tonne in early activity.

Overnight losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil accounted for some spillover selling pressure.

Canada exported 141,000 tonnes of canola during the week ended Nov. 15, which was roughly half of what moved the previous week, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.

However, marketing-year-to-date exports of 2.66 million tonnes remain well ahead of the 1.83 million tonnes exported by the same point in 2025-26.

Updated supply/demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada included only minor adjustments to the canola balance sheet, with projected 2026-27 ending stocks lowered to 1.87 million tonnes from 1.97 million in October.

Projected exports for the year were left unchanged at 7.7 million tonnes, while domestic usage was raised by 100,000 tonnes to 14.5 million.

About 14,300 canola contracts had traded as of 8:46 a.m. ET.

data.title: EU Open to 'Closest Possible Relationship' With U.K., Chief Says
data.description:
By Edith Hancock

The European Union is open to having a much closer relationship with the U.K., the head of the European Council said, as both sides continue work to thaw ties more than a decade after Britain voted to leave the bloc.

"We remain open to [having] the closest possible relationship between the European Union and the United Kingdom," European Council President Antonio Costa said Friday in Brussels.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was in the Belgian capital for a U.K.-EU summit to sign agreements on issues including youth mobility and food exports.

data.title: VEON 2026 Capital Markets Day Content is Now Available on Demand
data.description:
Full replay, presentation materials, and photo highlights from the November 16 event at Nasdaq MarketSite are available at veoncmd.com

New York and Dubai, November 20, 2026 – VEON Ltd. , a global digital operator, today announced that the full recording, presentation materials and photo highlights of its 2026 Capital Markets Day are now available on demand at veoncmd.com.

The event took place on November 16, 2026, at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York. The day opened with VEON’s management team ringing the Nasdaq Opening Bell to mark the 30th anniversary of the company’s US listing.

More than 50 external investors and analysts attended the Capital Markets Day that followed in person, and more than 70 further external participants joined the live webcast.

Under the vision “VEON 2030: A Better Life for All,” the company’s management team presented the Group’s strategy and its 2030 financial framework. This framework builds towards the following targets:

  • Growth: 12–15% organic annual growth in USD revenue and EBITDA, 2026 to 2030
  • Earnings and cash flow: earnings per share and free cash flow growing faster than revenue
  • Shareholder returns: at least USD 200 million annually, through share buybacks and cancellation
  • Balance sheet discipline: net leverage at or below 1.5x, excluding leases

VEON also aspires to increase its mix of digital services to approximately 50% of Group revenue by 2030, from 27.2% in the 3Q26, by combining organic growth with selective acquisitions. The Group’s 2030 growth target above is on an organic basis.

Kaan Terzioğlu, Group CEO at VEON said: “We were delighted by the strong engagement from investors and analysts, both in the room and online, at our Capital Markets Day 2026. During the event, we set out how telecom remains the foundation of our business, but it is not the destination. A year ago, digital services made up approximately a fifth of our revenue. Today it’s more than a quarter, and climbing every quarter we report. We’ve paired that growth with real capital discipline: raised guidance, an active share buyback, and a stronger balance sheet funding what comes next. For anyone who could not join us, the full presentations are now available, and we look forward to continuing the conversation with you as we build towards our next phase of growth.”

Explore the full Capital Markets Day at veoncmd.com

Visitors can access the full presentations and Q&A sessions, session materials, event highlights, and the VEON CEO’s AI Digital Twin - an interactive experience designed to help analysts and investors explore VEON’s published strategy and CMD content.

data.title: Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. to Open New Reiwatakiya Store at Westfield London, Strengthening Its Retail Presence in the UK
data.description:
Tokyo, Japan, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. (“Tokyo Lifestyle” or the “Company”) , a retailer and wholesaler of Japanese beauty and health products, sundry products, luxury products, electronic products, collectible cards, trendy toys as well as other products in Hong Kong, Japan, North America, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Kingdom and Australia, today announced the planned opening of a new store under its proprietary “Reiwatakiya” brand (the “Store”) in London, the United Kingdom, on November 21, 2026. This expansion marks another important milestone in the Company’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its UK retail presence, broaden its customer reach, and enhance its international sales network.

A Prime Retail Location in an Iconic Shopping Destination

Located at Westfield London, one of the largest shopping centers in the UK and Europe, the new Reiwatakiya Store is expected to benefit from substantial shopper traffic and a diverse international customer base. Supported by convenient transportation links, including underground, rail, and road networks, Westfield London and its surrounding area attract approximately 27.9 million visitors annually. The shopping center generates approximately £1 billion in annual retail sales, underscoring its position as a leading commercial and retail destination in London.

The Store will showcase Tokyo Lifestyle’s diverse selection of authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, selected Korean beauty brands. Strategically situated next to Zara and Apple stores, the Store is positioned to attract a broad consumer audience, particularly younger shoppers who represent an important target demographic for the Company.

To celebrate its grand opening on November 21 and 22, the Store will host special promotional activities, including a limited-time Japanese beauty goodie bag giveaway. These initiatives are designed to attract initial customer traffic, build brand awareness and foster engagement with local consumers. For more details about the grand opening event, please visit https://reiwatakiya.co.uk/.

The new Store will complement Tokyo Lifestyle’s existing London location in the city center, strengthening its retail presence in distinct commercial areas across the city. Together, these locations are expected to enhance the Company’s brand visibility, broaden its access to local consumers and international visitors, and provide a stronger operating foundation for potential expansion into other European markets.

Advancing Global Expansion Through a Distinctive Retail Brand Strategy

The Company’s UK expansion forms part of its broader global growth strategy, guided by its commitment to bringing authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, distinctive cultural experiences, and emerging consumer trends to customers worldwide. In recent years, Tokyo Lifestyle has accelerated the expansion of its international retail operations, with its latest physical store opening in Sydney in October 2026.

Alongside its expanding international retail footprint, the Company continues to pursue greater revenue diversification and brand development through a combination of directly operated stores, franchise partnerships, and wholesale distribution channels. These initiatives are intended to strengthen its international market presence, broaden its customer base, and establish a more diversified and scalable global business platform.

Mr. Mei Kanayama, Principal Executive Officer of Tokyo Lifestyle, commented: “The opening of our new Reiwatakiya store in the UK represents an important milestone in our long-term commitment to the UK and broader European markets. London has long served as a strategic gateway for our European expansion, and establishing two retail locations in distinct commercial areas across the city will enable us to reach a wider customer base, strengthen our brand recognition, and further develop our local operating capabilities.

“We have made a meaningful long-term commitment to this location, reflecting our confidence in the commercial potential of Westfield London and the continued appeal of Japanese beauty and lifestyle products among international consumers. Beyond adding another retail location, we see this Store as an opportunity to further refine our retail positioning, deepen customer engagement, and strengthen our understanding of local consumer preferences. Looking ahead, we intend to leverage our growing presence in London as a foundation for exploring additional opportunities across the UK and Europe, while continuing to build a distinctive and internationally recognized retail brand. We believe our expanding global retail network, combined with our diversified product portfolio and multi-channel business model, will position Tokyo Lifestyle to capture emerging market opportunities and generate sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.”

About Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd.

Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. (formerly known as Yoshitsu Co., Ltd) is a retailer and wholesaler of Japanese beauty and health products, sundry products, luxury products, electronic products, collectible cards, trendy toys, and other products in Hong Kong, Japan, North America, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Kingdom and Australia. The Company offers various beauty products (including cosmetics, skincare, fragrance, and body care products), health products (including over-the-counter drugs, nutritional supplements, and medical supplies and devices), sundry products (including home goods), collectible cards and trendy toys (including Pokémon cards, BE@RBRICK and other trendy products) and other products (including food and alcoholic beverages). The Company currently sells its products through directly-operated physical stores, through online stores, and to franchise stores and wholesale customers. data.title: FDA to miss deadline on Savara's rare lung disease drug approval
data.description:
Drug developer Savara said on Friday the US FDA would not meet its November 22 deadline to decide whether to approve the company's treatment for a rare lung disease, dealing a setback to the biotech firm.

Shares of the company were down 16% in premarket trading.

  • The US Food and Drug Administration did not provide a new date for a decision, Savara said, adding that its application for approval remains under review

  • The company is seeking approval of its experimental drug, molgramostim, for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), a rare condition in which material builds up in the lungs, making it harder for patients to breathe

  • Molgramostim is designed to help immune cells in the lungs clear that material. The drug is delivered through a nebulizer

data.title: Dealmaker Orcel's decades-long quest to shake up European banking
data.description:
By Valentina Za, John O'Donnell, Elvira Pollina and Tom Sims

Andrea Orcel had a point to prove in trying to redraw Europe's banking landscape, after notably failing at his first attempt with a blockbuster deal that led to the carve-up of ABN Amro nearly 20 years ago.

Victory this week in his two-year fight to take over Germany's Commerzbank marks the culmination of three decades of dealmaking for Orcel and puts the UniCredit CEO firmly at the centre of Europe's banking map.

"If you ask anybody, even any government, whether Europe needs larger or smaller banks, everybody will tell you larger banks," Orcel said on Thursday after a bitter bid battle which ranks as the largest cross-border banking operation in Europe since the global financial crisis.

The 63-year-old investment banking veteran had worked discreetly with a few trusted lieutenants to gain the upper hand by building up a position in Commerzbank that became so large that the Germans could no longer refuse to sit down with him.

People who have worked alongside Orcel describe the banker from Rome as a forceful and ambitious man who was undeterred by public rebukes in his pursuit of Commerzbank, landing a deal which successive UniCredit bosses had failed to deliver for decades.

Orcel arrived as chief executive at UniCredit in 2021, finally joining the Milan-headquartered bank which as a young Merrill Lynch banker he had helped build in 1998.

UniCredit had just lost the title of Italy's biggest bank to Intesa Sanpaolo , while Orcel was on the rebound after Spain's Santander dropped its offer to make him CEO in a dispute over pay in the wake of his exit from UBS .

Orcel relentlessly cut costs, shrank UniCredit's balance sheet to boost capital and favoured businesses that required less of it, returning billions to shareholders, helping to drive a tenfold increase in the bank's share price.

This gave Orcel a strong currency to pay for M&A, although with lessons of the financial crisis learned, he was at pains to reassure the bank's shareholders that he would never compromise their returns for the sake of a deal.

Only a few months into the job, Orcel broke off talks with Italy's government over the acquisition of Monte dei Paschi di Siena , damaging his credentials in Rome, where officials said he was too unpredictable to be relied on.

While relations with Rome have since improved, the initial blow-up over MPS came back to bite Orcel when from buying smaller domestic rival Banco BPM in 2025.

Interviews with a dozen current and former UniCredit employees and ex-UBS colleagues suggest Orcel mixes meticulous preparation with at times impulsive decision-making.

They also describe a restless and demanding executive who plays his cards close to his chest and keeps those around him constantly on their toes.

UniCredit declined to comment for this report.

Frustrated at home by the BPM setback, Orcel pivoted to Germany, where the year before he had built a stake in Commerzbank, sparking a backlash from management and staff at the country's second-largest lender as well as politicians and regulators.

"Many ask me why Germany. And the truth is that without Germany you can't really get anywhere. I'm very proud of being Italian: if the German locomotive stops, we stop," Orcel said this week after finally securing his Commerzbank goal with a deal with the government.

Tensions had reached boiling point in April when Orcel held an investor call during which he argued that Commerzbank was poorly run and set out his vision for how to fix the problem.

Angered by his attitude, German government officials refused to meet him, people with direct knowledge of the matter said.

Commerzbank Chairman Jens Weidmann, a highly respected former Bundesbank chief, ignored Orcel's insistent requests to meet for two years. He eventually relented in June and a month later said: "Everyone needs to act like adults now."

Orcel plans to remove both Weidmann and CEO Bettina Orlopp when the takeover of Frankfurt-based Commerzbank is complete.

Berlin and Commerzbank had not reckoned on how Orcel would use financial derivatives and exploit loopholes in Germany's takeover law to pull off the deal, a second person familiar with the situation said.

In the wake of Orcel's victory, Germany is now moving to change its takeover rules.

In order to reach his goal, Orcel borrowed the playbook of a major corporate client: the Berlusconi family's MFE broadcaster , whose own low-ball offer for Germany's ProSiebenSat.1 had been financed by UniCredit, a third person with knowledge of the matter said.

Orcel is the first to admit he eats, breathes and sleeps banks and banking.

"One should follow one's passions and I've always just liked banks," Orcel said this week.

"On a holiday in Mexico I told my wife-to-be: instead of the ruins, why don't we go take a look at the Mexican banks' branches?"

data.title: US Navy ship Wally Schirra docks at L&T Kattupalli for routine repairs
data.description:
The US Navy’s logistics ship, USNS Wally Schirra, arrived at L&T’s Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai on Friday for a “small voyage repair”, demonstrating the country’s growing maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) infrastructure and technical capabilities.

“The contract from US Navy’s Military Sealift Command (MSC) for Voyage Repair Availability (VRA) of USNS Wally Schirra which arrived at the dock on Friday morning is for a small voyage repair but successful execution of this order will help them undertake larger refits in India,” said sources privy to developments in L&T.

The VRA covers routine upkeep, minor hull or mechanical repairs, and emergent fixes performed pier side so the ship can quickly return to active service, elaborated sources.

Specialised Support

This marks the fifth occasion on which a US naval vessel has undertaken repairs at L&T’s modernised facility at Kattupalli under the India-US Master Ship Repair Agreement, as per a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

A Lewis and Clark-class dry cargo and ammunition ship, it provides ocean transportation, logistics and specialised maritime support to US military and government agencies worldwide.

India–US cooperation in ship repairs commenced from August 2022, when USNS Charles Drew became the first US Navy vessel to undergo repairs at an Indian shipyard. USNS Matthew Perry followed in March 2023 and USNS Salvor in July 2023.

As a fallout, L&T’s Kattupalli shipyard signed the Master Ship Repair Agreement with the US Navy in April 2023, institutionalising the cooperation and enabling the shipyard to undertake voyage repairs of US Navy vessels, MEA said.

USNS Charles Drew subsequently returned to Kattupalli for repairs in December 2024.

SOP Eased

Wally Schirra is the first US naval vessel to arrive for repairs after the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) was revised in July, facilitating smooth entry and exit of ship crew. The sector, otherwise, was burdened with long standing bureaucratic and visa bottlenecks regarding Shore Leave Passes (SLPs) and crew sign-on and sign-off procedures for civilian mariners and technicians arriving aboard vessels undergoing maintenance at Indian shipyards.

The revised SOP was finalised through coordinated efforts involving the MEA, Ministry of Home Affairs, Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Defence and Department of Defence Production, reflecting a whole-of-government approach towards facilitating ship-repair operations in India.

Other than the L&T, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) and Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) too have inked individual MSRAs with the US Navy between 2023 and 2024. Goa Shipyard Limited and Kolkata Port are also in advanced stages of negotiation for MSRAs.

MRO Potential

“With its strategic location along major international shipping routes, expanding shipyard infrastructure, skilled workforce and growing technical capabilities, India is well positioned to emerge as a hub for ship repair and maintenance across the Indo-Pacific and beyond,” observed the MEA.

The UK Royal Navy’s Royal Fleet Auxiliary (RFA) similarly has contracted Indian yards directly for mid-deployment upkeep, with two British auxiliary vessels have already availed MRO facilities for regular maintenance. Japan is also negotiating for a similar reciprocal pact.

data.title: Canada retail sales rise 0.8% in September; likely to be down 1.5% in October
data.description:
Key points:
  • October retail sales likely fall 1.5%, Statistics Canada says
  • Core retail sales edge up 0.1% in September
  • Gasoline station and fuel vendor sales jump 6.9% in September

By Promit Mukherjee

Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% in September on a monthly basis to C$75.31 billion ($52.58 billion), slightly more than expectations as sales picked up at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, Statistics Canada said on Friday.

The September growth rate was lower than the upwardly revised 1.4% growth in August, and the statistics agency said in a preliminary estimate that sales were likely to be down 1.5% in October.

  • Retail sales, which include purchases of cars, furniture, food and gasoline, are considered an early indicator of gross domestic product growth and account for about 40% of consumer spending

  • Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors and motor vehicle and parts dealers, edged up 0.1% in September, representing 66.9% of retail trade

  • In August, retail sales were higher in five out of nine subsectors. In volume terms, retail sales were up 0.1% in the month

  • Sales at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, which contribute almost a tenth of the total retail sales in the country, were the biggest contributor with 6.9% growth in September

  • Sales of motor vehicles and parts, which is by far the biggest contributor to overall sales and accounts for over a quarter of overall sales, were up 0.2%

  • Sales at food and beverage retailers, the second biggest contributor to retail sales, were down 0.4% in the month

  • The categories of building material and furniture retailers were both down 1.3%, data showed

data.title: The Dow joins the correction watch
data.description:
Key points:
  • US equity index futures red; Nasdaq 100 down ~1.5%
  • STOXX 600 index slides >1.5%
  • Dollar falls; gold down >1%; US crude slips; bitcoin rises
  • US 10-year Treasury yield falls to ~4.99%

THE DOW JOINS THE CORRECTION WATCH

With the Nasdaq Composite , Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 already in correction territory, traders are increasingly watching to see whether the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and Dow Jones Industrial Average follow suit.

The S&P 500 ended Thursday down 8.2% from its October 6 record close, while the Dow finished 9.7% below its August 5 peak, leaving the blue-chip average just a small step away from the 10% correction threshold.

The Dow's recent decline has accelerated since the November 3 midterm elections and is on track for its biggest monthly drop since March. The index has also fallen four straight days and is headed for its worst weekly loss since the tariff-driven selloff in early April 2025.

Technically, this week's weakness is significant because the Dow has broken below a rising channel that had guided the advance from the spring lows. The average ended Thursday at 49,097.06.

While E-mini Dow futures (YMcv1) are modestly lower ahead of Friday's open, volatility has surged. The Cboe Volatility Index has climbed above 31 and reached its highest level since late March, underscoring heightened uncertainty and the potential for sharp swings in the major indexes.

The Dow’s next key support zone lies in the 48,757-48,708 area, where the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement of the March-August advance aligns closely with the April 29 low.

If that area fails, attention could shift toward the 47,343-47,130 region. That zone includes the maximum Fibonacci retracement range of the March-August rally and lies just above an unfilled April gap that requires a fall to 46,744 for a fill. A decline into this area would leave the Dow roughly 13%-14% below its record high.

A complete round trip to the March 30 intraday low near 45,057 would leave the Dow down more than 17% from its record close.

On the upside, resistance sits near 49,900. More importantly, a recovery above the 50,550-51,050 area, which includes the 200-day moving average and several key chart markers, would suggest the Dow has at least stabilized for now.

data.title: Gold, Silver Drop to Lowest Levels in Over a Year — Update
data.description:
By Megan Cheah and Farhan Rafid

Gold and silver prices fell to their lowest levels in over a year on Friday as a broader selloff across commodities and expectations of higher interest rates globally pressured precious metals.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for gold as a safe haven for risk-averse investors. The precious metals weakened despite heavy losses across Asian stock markets.

December gold futures fell 3.4% to $3,561.70 a troy ounce, while spot silver declined around 2.1% to $41.84 an ounce.

The decline in precious metals is part of a broader selloff across commodities, with investors cutting exposure, unwinding crowded positions and taking profits ahead of year-end, according to Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.

Hansen said in a note Friday that precious metals had suffered the largest losses, with silver falling 14% and gold nearly 8% this week. Rising borrowing costs, a stronger U.S. dollar and concerns about artificial-intelligence investment have added to selling pressure, while losses in other assets have increased demand for cash.

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity-market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Hansen said. However, holdings in gold exchange-traded funds have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure.

The gold-to-silver ratio rose as high as 85.65 Friday, about 25% above its average over nearly three decades. The ratio measures how many ounces of silver are needed to buy an ounce of gold, with a higher reading indicating silver is relatively cheaper.

Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke said silver's decline below $45 an ounce, alongside a gold-to-silver ratio above 85, could present a buying opportunity. However, the bank is waiting for signs that prices have bottomed before turning more positive, as further declines remain possible. Julius Baer maintains a neutral view on silver and a constructive outlook for gold.

Copper also declined, with December futures falling 2.4% to $5.4965 a pound. The industrial metal is on track to lose around 9% this week, reaching an eight-month low amid concerns about global growth, Chinese demand and the outlook for artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment, according to Saxo Bank.

Julius Baer upgraded its outlook for copper to constructive following the recent correction, saying the metal remains at risk of a structural supply deficit as demand from electric vehicles, clean energy and battery storage increases. Copper prices have fallen more than 15% from their highs this year, but the bank expects electrification-related technologies to account for around 30% of demand by 2035, compared with 25% in 2025. Menke said mining investments are increasing but might come too late to prevent a shortage.

Japan's consumer inflation data for October, released Friday, showed prices were accelerating past the Bank of Japan's target. That reinforced expectations for tighter policy as policymakers grew increasingly worried about the risk of higher prices due to increased energy costs, persistent yen weakness and rising semiconductor prices amid the artificial-intelligence boom.

"A rate hike at the next meeting in December looks highly likely, and the central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to accelerate into the 3% range," said Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute.

Minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, also showed that nearly all policymakers expected higher interest rates would be needed to lower inflation.

The minutes "showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG analysts. Markets recently priced in a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Many also expect the European Central Bank to raise rates in December after staying on hold last month, as it is under pressure to address the inflationary backdrop given persistently high energy prices.

A higher interest-rate environment typically diminishes the allure of nonyielding assets such as gold and silver. The hawkish Fed view also likely lifted the dollar, which makes gold and silver--both dollar-denominated commodities--more expensive for investors holding other currencies.

Upcoming U.S. economic data could shape expectations for the size of a December interest-rate move by the Fed, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage in a note. This includes the second estimate for the country's third-quarter gross domestic product growth due next week.

"Firm readings could lift yields further and extend gold's losses, while softer prints may offer some relief," he added.

data.title: Saudi Arabia once banned Grand Theft Auto. Now it's got a stake in it
data.description:
Key points:
  • Saudi investments in gaming part of push to move beyond oil
  • Sovereign wealth fund PIF a major backer of firm behind GTA
  • Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman an avid gamer
  • Authorities eased gaming restrictions on GTA in 2025

By Nazih Osseiran and Mohammed Benmansour

Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being embraced not only by its gamers - a category that includes Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman - but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs.

This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon launch — the first new release of the top-selling series since a Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025.

"Playing GTA VI in Saudi Arabia legally makes me so happy, because we're talking about a game that was banned," local content creator Thamer al Dairem said from a windowless, air-conditioned room, lit mostly by the bank of monitors displaying the game.

"We're talking about the biggest game in the world."

Support and investment in gaming by Saudi Arabia have been rising fast, not least from de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, often known by his initials MBS, who told Fox News in 2023 that gaming helped him disconnect and let off steam.

The Public Investment Fund (PIF), the sovereign wealth fund he chairs, owns a major stake worth over $2 billion in Take-Two Interactive , the US firm that owns Grand Theft Auto-developer Rockstar Games, LSEG Workspace data show.

CHANGING CUSTOMS IN CONSERVATIVE SAUDI ARABIA

In August, a consortium including PIF acquired gaming giant Electronic Arts for $55 billion. This month, gaming software provider Unity Software held talks with investors including the Saudi sovereign wealth fund on a potential buyout valuing it at around $25 billion.

PIF, which has spent the past year consolidating its gaming holdings into a subsidiary, Savvy Games Group, declined to comment.

MBS has been leading a campaign to open Saudi Arabia up and ease strict social and cultural norms that revolve around a conservative interpretation of Islam — a far cry from GTA VI's Vice City.

GTA VI advertisements have been appearing in some of Saudi Arabia's most popular shopping malls. One image shows the heroine wearing shorts and a crop top, her arm resting on her partner's shoulder — unthinkable a few years ago, when women were required to dress modestly and cover their hair.

MBS's wider reform plan, dubbed Vision 2030, is all about reducing reliance on oil and gas revenues, both in the economy and in state revenues, and PIF strategy is part of that.

"(It) is part of a diversified long-term investment strategy to capture value from industries it does not traditionally operate within," said Piers Harding-Rolls, who researches games at Ampere Analysis.

In Riyadh, al Dairem is now streaming Grand Theft Auto content and says that, while some of the depictions of violence, drugs and sex are extreme, the game is age-restricted and reflects another country.

"The city is Vice City, and it's representing Miami and the chaotic things that happen. For us Saudis, like, we know that it has nothing to do with us."

The gaming experience, on the other hand, matters hugely to him.

"When I saw the ads of GTA VI in the malls, I was so happy. If you'd asked me if I was ever going to see this, like, 10 years ago in Saudi, I wouldn't have believed it."
